metadata.name: Liver Disease (10-year)
metadata.description: 10-year risk of NAFLD progression to cirrhosis and liver-related mortality. Progression driven by metabolic syndrome components (obesity, diabetes, dyslipidemia)

caseFatality10yr.basis: Medicare real-world cohort: 31.1% cumulative mortality over ~8 years with NAFLD compensated cirrhosis
caseFatality10yr.citation: Loomba R, Wong R, Fraysse J, et al. The natural history of NAFLD with advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis. Aliment Pharmacol Ther 2020;51(11):1149-1159

curves.notes: NAFLD to cirrhosis progression 1-5%/year; depends on fibrosis stage and metabolic factors
NAFLD to cirrhosis progression 1-5%/year; depends on fibrosis stage and metabolic factors

riskFactors.name: FIB-4 Score (Derived from Age, AST, ALT, Platelets)
riskFactors.citation: Fibrosis-4 Index as an Independent Predictor of Mortality and Liver-Related Outcomes in NAFLD. Hepatol Commun. 2022;6(4):765-779
riskFactors.notes: FIB-4 >=2.67: all-cause mortality HR 2.49 (2.20-2.82), cirrhosis HR 2.04, HCC HR 3.66; separate cohort: liver events aHR 16.5 for FIB-4 >2.67 vs <1.30 (10-yr cumulative incidence 15% vs 1%).

riskFactors.name: Body Mass Index
riskFactors.citation: Jarvis H, Craig D, Barker R, et al. Metabolic risk factors and incident advanced liver disease in NAFLD: systematic review and meta-analysis of population-based observational studies. PLoS Med. 2020;17(4):e1003100
riskFactors.notes: Obesity: pooled aHR 1.20 (1.12-1.28) for incident advanced liver disease; largest single cohort (UKCTOCS) HR 2.25 (1.70-2.97) anchors the severe-obesity end.

riskFactors.name: Type 2 Diabetes
riskFactors.citation: Jarvis H, Craig D, Barker R, et al. Metabolic risk factors and incident advanced liver disease in NAFLD. PLoS Med. 2020;17(4):e1003100
riskFactors.notes: T2DM: adjusted HR 2.25 (1.83-2.76) for incident severe liver disease (12 studies, 22.8M participants).

riskFactors.name: Dyslipidemia (High Triglycerides, Low HDL)
riskFactors.citation: Jarvis H, Craig D, Barker R, et al. Metabolic risk factors and incident advanced liver disease in NAFLD. PLoS Med. 2020;17(4):e1003100
riskFactors.notes: High triglycerides HR 1.30 (0.99-1.72, borderline); combined dyslipidemia HR 1.23 (1.19-1.28); low HDL 1.28 (1.04-1.59). Capped ~1.4 accordingly.

riskFactors.name: Alcohol Consumption
riskFactors.citation: How does alcohol use impact morbidity and mortality of liver cirrhosis? A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis (44 studies, 5.1M participants). Hepatol Int. 2023;17:1339-1351
riskFactors.notes: Cirrhosis mortality dose-response: RR 2.65 at 25 g/day (~12 US drinks/week), 6.83 at 50 g/day (~25/week), 16.38 at 100 g/day (~50/week).

riskFactors.name: NAFLD or NASH Diagnosis
riskFactors.citation: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease and mortality from all causes, cardiovascular disease, and cancer: a meta-analysis. Sci Rep. 2019;9:11124
riskFactors.notes: NAFLD with significant fibrosis/cirrhosis: mortality HR 3.22 (2.40-4.33); NAFLD alone HR 1.34 (1.17-1.54). Diagnosis within a liver-progression model weighted toward the fibrosis estimate.

riskFactors.name: Cirrhosis Diagnosis
riskFactors.citation: Fleming KM, et al. All-cause mortality in people with cirrhosis compared with the general population: a population-based cohort study. Liver Int. 2012;32(1):79-84
riskFactors.notes: Compensated cirrhosis HR 4.7 (4.4-5.0) vs general population; decompensated 9.7 (8.9-10.6).
